title: Kali desktop and Android Wi-Fi connection prepared
summary: Installed the missing XFCE desktop, verified real authenticated desktop pixels, and added same-network app access; firewall activation and phone checks remain pending.

changes.detail: Initial desktop tests found the recommended XFCE desktop absent, then a read-only WSLg X11 socket mount. Installed kali-desktop-xfce and applied the same socket mount preparation as Win-KeX; authenticated framebuffer test now passes.

Native Live Kali Wi-Fi screen embeds the owner-gated local app in a WebView restricted to a selected private IPv4 origin on port 8081. Added /kali web route, desktop fullscreen and reconnect, exact-host LAN opt-in and reusable server launcher.

Prepared Android version 1.0.5/build 7 with a new OTA runtime and local WebView HTTP support. Normal production owner API still requires HTTPS. Wi-Fi traffic uses HTTP and must be limited to a trusted local network. No firewall rule was created, no public tunnel or deployment; no source files removed.

validation.name: Kali desktop and terminal tests
validation.detail: All 12 tests passed: private-host restrictions, origin-bound expiring single-use tickets, owner isolation, VNC-only security, real VNC password authentication and pixel transfer, desktop stop, and existing PowerShell/Python/Node/Kali terminal behavior.

validation.name: App checks
validation.detail: App TypeScript and focused ESLint passed before the final lifecycle/theme refinements; six history interaction/persistence tests passed. Final check rerun pending.

validation.name: Local HTTP
validation.detail: Local /kali returned 200. Desktop API rejected unauthenticated requests with OWNER_LOGIN_REQUIRED and external origins with LOCAL_LAB_ONLY; local CORS preflight returned 204.

validation.name: Build and activation
validation.detail: APK offline build failed because Kotlin plugin 2.2.0 was not cached; online retry pending. Root typecheck corrections pending verification. Automatic approval review rejected opening TCP 3002/3003/8081 to the Wi-Fi subnet and restarting in LAN mode until the user explicitly approves that exposure. No connected phone or available browser automation surface; no device/visual verification.
